factūrus sum

the future participle, agreeing with the subject, with sum

I am going to do, I am about to do

What someone means to do or is on the point of doing; in the past, factūrus eram, I was going to. The plain future says only that it will happen (see will).

Other words

  • in eō est ut (+ subjunctive) — it is just about to happen

    impersonal phrase, with ut and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Liv. 2.17.5: cum jam in eō esset, ut in mūrōs ēvāderet mīles (Lewis & Short)

    Of a thing on the very point of happening, mostly in narrative: “the soldiers were just about to scale the walls”.

Examples

  • quid agis, quid āctūrus es?

    What are you doing? What are you going to do?Plin. Ep. 9.32

  • dictūrus sum canticum quod nōvī

    I am going to recite a song I knowAug. Conf. 11.28.38

  • quidnam futūrum est, sī creārit līberōs?

    What is going to happen if he has children?Phaedr. 1.6.9

  • crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper

    “Tomorrow I’m going to live,” you say, Postumus, always “tomorrow”Mart. 5.58.1

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē

    we expect to come to Tusculum on the Nones or the day afterCic. Fam. 14.20.1

  • factūrusne operae pretium sim … nec satis sciō

    whether I am going to do something worth the effort, I don’t really knowLiv. praef. 1

See also will, future, would.
